item.title: Brittany Renner Responds To Courtside Outfit Backlash With A Question
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Brittany Renner responds on X after her courtside appearance with Celina Powell draws attention at the Clippers game.
item.content:encoded:
Brittany Renner responded to the backlash over her revealing courtside outfit by posing a question on X after attending the Clippers-Thunder game.

“Who wears this to a game…” Renner wrote in a November 14 post on X. Her verified account had drawn more than 641,000 views and 4,500 likes on the response by Sunday.

Renner attended the November 13 matchup at Intuit Dome with Celina Powell. The pair wore revealing black outfits, and a photograph of Renner near the courtside seats circulated alongside footage from the arena.

The picture, credited to Los Angeles Times photographer Wally Skalij, also captured spectators seated behind her. One woman appeared with her mouth open as Renner passed the row, prompting comments about the background of the photograph as well as her clothing.

The courtside outfit contrasted with her covered-up appearance at the June 2025 BET Awards, where she wore a head covering and a long dress. Renner had publicly embraced Islam before removing her hijab that month; by July 2026, she said she was no longer practicing the religion.

At the May 2, 2025, “Basketball Wives” premiere, Renner spoke publicly about embracing Islam. She told PEOPLE she had considered the faith for years before taking her Shahada, the declaration of faith.

“I felt like if I had not taken my Shahada, I was gonna go down a really dark road,” Renner told PEOPLE in that interview.

In a June 2025 interview with Bootleg Kev, Renner said she and Kevin Gates married April 6 and ended their marriage May 28. “I gave 100 percent,” Renner said. “All is well.”

She discussed that 52-day marriage and split during BET Awards weekend. REAL 92.3 LA posted the conversation June 7, 2025.

By June 18, 2025, she was posting her uncovered natural hair. TheJasmineBRAND’s contemporaneous report reproduced her Instagram caption: “I don’t have blind loyalty to any person, place, or thing.” Renner also wrote, “It’s still Alhamdulillah for everything!”

In January 2026, Hollywood Unlocked transcribed her explanation of what covering up had meant during that period. “And Islam provided that protection I needed while I was rebuilding myself,” Renner said in a “Facets Of Life With Brittany” clip.

Her later comments addressed religion directly. In July 2026, Hip-HopVibe reported that Renner said she no longer practiced Islam and wasn’t following any religion, after also undergoing a baptism. “No. I’m not in practice anymore,” Renner said when asked whether she was still Muslim, according to that report.

The Clippers beat the Thunder 113-112.

Replies under Renner’s post included a joke from @ClippPaul2X: “her first time seeing the moon up close 😭”

Another user, @jr5mics, wrote, “I had a feeling it was you.”

item.title: T-Boz’s Daughter Chase Rolison Recalls Memory Loss During Lupus Hospitalization
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: T-Boz's daughter Chase Rolison opens up about a frightening hospital stay, recovery and the work she still wants to pursue.
item.content:encoded:
T-Boz‘s daughter Chase Rolison says a lupus hospitalization last year left her struggling to remember weeks of her life and working to regain basic movement. The fashion entrepreneur described the ordeal during an interview with Reginae Carter.

Chase, whose father is Mack 10, said she initially believed the hospital stay had lasted only a few days. In the conversation on Carter’s YouTube channel, she recalled a much longer stretch and a difficult recovery.

“I like lost my memory for that whole month. I don’t even remember. I thought I was in the hospital for three days. I was in there for like 20 something days,” Chase said.

She said sitting up could take her half an hour and that she had to learn to walk again. Discussing the severity of her health struggles, Chase added, “I’ve almost lost my life three times.”

Chase credited her mother’s openness about living with sickle cell disease with helping her prepare for her own health challenges. Growing up, she accompanied T-Boz on hospital visits and watched how the TLC singer handled her condition.

T-Boz’s health has also affected TLC’s touring schedule. Last month, Chilli updated concertgoers on her recovery while continuing to perform without her.

Chase told Carter her symptoms can change from one day to the next, disrupting both plans and work. She said people who have not experienced serious health problems themselves, or known someone who has, do not always understand those limits.

“So, it’s like I can’t always go to everything I want to go to or do certain things I really want to do or like, you know what I’m saying?” Chase said.

The conversation also covered Anela Vintage, the clothing business Chase has built around late-1990s and early-2000s styles. She said its name comes from her middle name and described an appointment-based showroom in West Hollywood.

Her interest in fashion stretches back to childhood shopping trips and working on clothes with her mother. Chase said she also wants to move beyond selling vintage pieces and begin designing her own.

Chase’s longer-term goal is to open a store on Melrose.

item.title: Diddy & Accuser Seek Five-Month Delay In Lawsuit Claiming He Dangled Her Over 17th-Floor Balcony
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Diddy and his civil accuser ask for more preparation time, citing unfinished depositions and obstacles to prison communication.
item.content:encoded:
Diddy and Bryana Bongolan both want their civil trial pushed to November 2027, citing unfinished witness questioning and prison communication restrictions.

Their November 11 joint filing asks a Los Angeles federal judge to replace the June 8, 2027 trial date with November 9. The parties’ proposed five-month postponement and revised pretrial calendar are subject to the court’s approval.

Lawyers for both sides say working with Diddy in custody has slowed document review and defense preparation.

They also cite the coordination needed between the rapper and his corporate co-defendants, Bad Boy Entertainment LLC and CeOpco LLC.

The parties wrote that imprisonment “has created significant practical difficulties in communicating with him, as well as coordinating his defense strategy and review of relevant documents.”

Bongolan’s allegations concern a September 2016 encounter at Cassie Ventura’s Los Angeles apartment. She says Diddy sexually assaulted her, held her over a 17th-floor balcony and threw her onto patio furniture. He has denied the accusations.

Bongolan’s attorneys previously changed the alleged timeline. As AllHipHop reported, they revised the date to a broader September 2016 period, rather than a specific day, after the defense challenged her account using travel and performance records.

Her amended complaint also included messages in which Ventura described the alleged confrontation to Diddy’s former chief of staff, Kristina Khorram. Bongolan separately testified about the balcony allegation during his criminal trial in June 2025.

The latest request says the civil litigation still faces an unresolved dismissal motion filed March 6. The defendants argue that some claims were brought too late and that others do not adequately state a legal claim.

Because that motion remains pending, the defense has not answered the second amended complaint, according to the joint filing.

Both sides say they need more time for written discovery and depositions of essential witnesses.

Their proposed calendar would move the fact-discovery cutoff and mandatory settlement conference from November 20, 2026, to April 23, 2027. They describe this as their first request to continue the trial and say they have pursued preparation as circumstances allowed.

The proposed deadline for completing expert discovery would become July 8, 2027.

item.title: Tia Kemp Says Son Didn’t Call Cops After Gunman Campus Attack
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Tia Kemp recounts the drive home and the decision her son made when an armed confrontation threatened to turn deadly.
item.content:encoded:
Tia Kemp says her son chose not to fight back when an armed man confronted him, then drove hours home before telling her what had happened.

In a November 13 interview with Cam Newton, Kemp described the moment she learned about the alleged attack on William Roberts III, her son with Rick Ross. Her account adds a mother’s perspective to the October 11 incident near Bethune-Cookman University in Daytona Beach.

Kemp said she had just returned from a flight when her son arrived with bloodshot eyes and told her someone had threatened him and hit him with a gun. “I dropped to my knees,” Kemp told Newton.

She said Roberts wanted her to call his father, but she wanted to establish whether police had been contacted. “He didn’t call his dad. He didn’t call me. He didn’t call the police,” Kemp said of his initial response.

According to Kemp, women who were with her son contacted authorities instead. She said he went to his apartment, then left for home rather than stay nearby.

Kemp also pushed back on descriptions suggesting a prolonged beating. She said the man struck Roberts once and that he did not suffer a gash. Her concern, she explained, was that any attempt to retaliate could have led to a shooting.

She credited her son’s discipline with helping him avoid that confrontation. In her telling, Roberts backed away without answering the threat and waited for the armed man to leave.

She said the confrontation involved a woman her son had been seeing for roughly a month. AllHipHop previously reported that police noted slight swelling and that Roberts declined medical attention. He identified a suspect in a photo lineup, while investigators found no footage of the attack on city cameras.

The incident also disrupted his education. By October 28, Kemp said he was taking classes online after she brought him home and did not want him returning to campus.

Kemp mentioned police body-camera recordings during the interview. That is distinct from the surveillance footage investigators sought of the alleged assault itself; her remarks did not establish that the attack was recorded.

The police account placed the confrontation at McLeod Avenue and Weaver Street.

item.title: Jay Electronica Backs Land Fundraiser For Proposed Youth Village
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Jay Electronica's New York benefit will support land acquisition for the proposed Mother Khadijah's Discovery Village.
item.content:encoded:
Jay Electronica is using his next New York show to help raise money for land for a proposed youth campus. His November 15 benefit at The Town Hall will support the proposed Mother Khadijah’s Discovery Village, organizers said.

The concert website says a portion of every ticket will support land acquisition, the project’s opening phase. It describes a development vision exceeding $15 million, with Gary, Indiana, and Chicago listed as proposed locations.

Organizers are targeting fall 2029 for the campus and describe a mix of education, athletics and family activities. Their plans include technology labs, urban agriculture and workforce programs alongside recreation for young people.

The November concert also gives ticket holders a new date after an earlier postponement. Ticketmaster’s event notice identifies August 7 as the previous date, while The Town Hall’s current listing confirms the benefit is now set for November 15.

Young performers would also have a place in the proposed campus, which includes a 1,000-seat theater and studio spaces. Financial literacy, entrepreneurship, digital skills and family recreation are also part of the plan described on the benefit website.

The Town Hall lists Women Working Together Globally as the presenter and confirms the November 15 date. Its event page describes support for STEM education, mental health, healthy living, anti-bullying efforts, technology access and sports.

The project carries a name already attached to decades of activities for children.

Mother Khadijah Farrakhan’s Children’s Village has been part of the Nation of Islam’s annual Saviours’ Day gatherings since the 1990s, bringing families together for recreation and learning.

In 2025, that gathering took place at Up Your Alley in Schererville, Indiana, rather than inside the convention itself. Children bowled, played laser tag and arcade games, and selected books and toys from a gift room.

That history gives the proposed permanent campus a connection to an existing tradition, rather than an entirely new youth program.

The concert arrives months after Khadijah Farrakhan died at 90 in June, following 72 years of marriage to Louis Farrakhan.

Jay Electronica’s November 15 performance is scheduled for The Town Hall at 123 West 43rd Street in Manhattan.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Suno Faces Demand To Open New AI Models To Copyright Discovery
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Suno wants its second major-label case paused, but Universal and Sony seek records on newer models and business activity.
item.content:encoded:
Suno‘s bid to pause a major copyright lawsuit has run into demands for answers about its newest music-making technology. Universal and Sony labels want discovery into newer models to continue while ownership questions involving more than 60,000 recordings wait.

The labels outlined that compromise in a November 13 filing in Massachusetts federal court. They want records about model training, licensing negotiations, business expansion and finances rather than a freeze covering the entire case.

“Delay would not merely postpone building the record, it would degrade it,” the labels’ attorneys wrote. They argue that engineers could leave and technical knowledge could become harder to reconstruct as Suno keeps developing new products.

Their concern includes v6, which they say has not received full scrutiny in the earlier lawsuit. They also offer reciprocal information about licensing markets and the effect of AI-generated music on their recordings.

Suno takes a different view of what should happen before the second case advances. Its October 30 motion argues that decisions in the original lawsuit could resolve claims or narrow the evidence needed here.

That first case began in June 2024 with allegations involving 560 recordings. When the labels sought to add more than 60,000 works, the judge declined to expand it and directed them toward a parallel lawsuit.

The second complaint followed in September, with Suno answering it in October and asserting fair use among its defenses. Suno says it is preserving relevant material and argues that proceeding now would impose unnecessary expense on both sides. The company also contends that a favorable ruling could eliminate the need to examine ownership of those recordings.

The company’s discovery disputes also reach investors outside the Massachusetts case. NVentures has separately sought to block testimony demanded by the labels after producing more than 28,000 pages, arguing that Suno should answer questions about its own operations.

The labels’ latest proposal would carry evidence from the first case into the second without repeating the same work. If the judge orders a broader pause, they alternatively seek a preservation order covering training data and engineering records.

Motions seeking judgment before trial in the original lawsuit are due June 22, 2027.

item.title: Ice Cube’s BIG3 Hires PepsiCo Veteran To Build Media Business
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ice Cube brings Adam Harter aboard BIG3 as the league looks at new entertainment formats while its public merger remains pending.
item.content:encoded:
Ice Cube is putting a former PepsiCo executive in charge of growing BIG3’s business beyond the basketball court.

Adam Harter became president of business operations on November 12, with media strategy and new markets among his responsibilities. The league also wants to explore documentaries and unscripted programming.

“Nine seasons in, the BIG3 has never been bigger. Eight cities, a global footprint, and 3-on-3 is on the Olympic stage,” said Ice Cube, Co-Founder and CEO of the BIG3. “As we head into our milestone 10th season, we’re building a business to match what’s happening on the court. Adam has done it at the highest level, and he understands our fans. He’s here to help us go get it.”

Harter will answer to Cube and co-founder Jeff Kwatinetz while overseeing partnerships, marketing and live events.

His resume includes more than 22 years at PepsiCo and a stint as LIV Golf’s chief marketing officer. At PepsiCo, Harter worked on branded entertainment, including the feature film Uncle Drew, bringing production experience alongside sports sponsorship work.

BIG3 previously pursued a television project in 2023, when Ice Cube was attached to star in and produce a docuseries about the league. That announced concept followed a team’s championship pursuit while exploring the work of establishing the competition and its dispute with Qatari investors.

The earlier project was described by comparing it to Welcome to Wrexham and Cheer, two series built around sports organizations. The new announcement names possible programming formats rather than announcing a completed show, buyer or premiere date.

The executive change also comes during BIG3’s planned merger with Graf Global, announced in June with a $290 million valuation before new funding. Under those terms, existing equity and equity-linked interests would become shares in the combined business upon closing.

The June rollout identified franchises in Los Angeles, Houston, Dallas, Chicago, Detroit, Boston, Miami and the Washington-area DMV. Its coaching lineup included Nancy Lieberman, Gary Payton and Julius Erving, with former NBA players such as Dwight Howard and Michael Beasley among the league’s competitors.

AllHipHop previously reported that completion required shareholder and regulatory approvals, an exchange listing and at least $50 million in net cash proceeds. The latest league announcement still describes the transaction as pending rather than a completed stock-market debut.

Harter will work with Sean Bannon, who holds the separate position of president of league operations.

item.title: Wu-Tang Clan’s RZA Reflects On Rock Hall Honor: ‘It’s A Long Journey’
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wu-Tang Clan's RZA reflects on the group's journey in a Rock Hall red-carpet interview as its 2026 induction arrives.
item.content:encoded:
Wu-Tang Clan‘s RZA reflected on the group’s path to the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in a red-carpet interview released by the institution Sunday.

“It’s a long journey,” RZA said in the Rock Hall’s interview. The group joined the 2026 class in the performer category after appearing on the nomination ballot for the first time.

The group’s performance included “C.R.E.A.M.” and “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit,” AFP reported from the ceremony.

Ahead of the event, ODB’s widow, Icelene Jones, said Young Dirty Bastard would represent his father. The ceremony fell one day after the anniversary of ODB’s November 13, 2004 death.

“Wu-Tang rewrote the rules of hip-hop and did it without a big machine behind them,” Chris Rock said while inducting the group.

Steve Rifkind responded in an Instagram post, asking Rock to apologize to Loud’s staff. “you owe the staff of Loud apology for what you said,” he wrote.

Wu-Tang’s agreement with Loud Records allowed members to make solo deals elsewhere, rather than placing every album with one company.

Before securing that deal, the rappers pooled money to record “Protect Ya Neck.” Each MC contributed $50, and the group promoted the single through radio visits and direct sales while traveling between states.

Their debut, “Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers),” arrived in 1993. RZA’s production combined soul samples, martial-arts film dialogue and sparse percussion beneath the members’ contrasting voices.

Solo projects followed, including Method Man’s “Tical,” Raekwon’s “Only Built 4 Cuban Linx…” and GZA’s “Liquid Swords.” Ghostface Killah released “Ironman” in 1996, while ODB’s “Return to the 36 Chambers: The Dirty Version” arrived in 1995.

The group reunited on record for “Wu-Tang Forever” in 1997. Its opening-week sales of roughly 612,000 copies put the double album at No. 1.

Wu-Tang also expanded into clothing through Wu-Wear. Later group albums included “The W” in 2000, “Iron Flag” in 2001 and “8 Diagrams” in 2007.

Their beginnings reached television through Hulu’s “Wu-Tang: An American Saga,” with Shameik Moore portraying Raekwon. Documentary filmmaker Sacha Jenkins approached the same history through interviews and archival material.

Showtime acquired North American rights to Jenkins’ series in January 2019.

item.title: Queen Latifah & MC Lyte Bring ‘U.N.I.T.Y.’ & ‘Ruffneck’ To Rock Hall
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Queen Latifah accepted her Rock Hall honor from Megan Thee Stallion, then performed a joint medley with MC Lyte.
item.content:encoded:
Queen Latifah entered the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Saturday with Megan Thee Stallion delivering her induction. She then joined MC Lyte for a medley featuring “U.N.I.T.Y.” and “Ruffneck.”

The Associated Press reported that both women accepted Early Influence honors at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater. Remy Ma inducted Lyte.

Megan and Latifah previously performed “U.N.I.T.Y.” together at Coachella in April 2025.

Megan has also discussed modeling her acting ambitions after Latifah. During her appearance on Michelle Obama’s “IMO” podcast, she described Latifah as both a mentor and a friend.

The songs in Saturday’s performance date to 1993, when both rappers released records that earned Grammy recognition. Lyte’s “Ruffneck” received a nomination, while Latifah’s “U.N.I.T.Y.” won Best Rap Solo Performance in 1995.

Latifah released “U.N.I.T.Y.” on “Black Reign,” her third album. The song addressed harassment, domestic violence and misogyny, following the women-centered message of “Ladies First” from her 1989 debut, “All Hail the Queen.”

Before that debut, a 1988 demo led to Latifah’s Tommy Boy deal after she had learned to beatbox and rap with the Ladies Fresh crew.

Lyte released “Lyte as a Rock” in 1988 and followed it with “Eyes on This” in 1989. That same year, she participated in the Stop the Violence Movement’s “Self Destruction,” alongside artists including KRS-One.

They shared another tribute stage in 2023 during “A Grammy Salute to 50 Years of Hip-Hop.” Latifah performed “Ladies First” with Monie Love, and a larger group including Lyte, Remy Ma and Latto closed the women’s segment with “U.N.I.T.Y.”

The two also built careers outside recording. Lyte has worked as a DJ, actress and television announcer, while Latifah moved into “Living Single” and “Set It Off” before earning an Oscar nomination for “Chicago.”

Latifah later recorded soul and jazz standards on 2004’s “The Dana Owens Album,” then returned to rap with 2009’s “Persona.” She received a Kennedy Center Honor in 2023 alongside Billy Crystal, Renee Fleming, Barry Gibb and Dionne Warwick.

“It wasn’t always popular, but it was always worth it, you know,” Latifah said in the Rock Hall’s red-carpet interview.

Lyte cofounded the Hip Hop Sisters Network in 2006 to promote positive images of women and youth from diverse backgrounds.

item.title: Cam’ron Says His Career Isn’t Big Enough For A Super Bowl Show
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cam'ron sizes up his catalog against the Super Bowl stage and explains why a call from Jay-Z wouldn't change his answer.
item.content:encoded:
Cam’ron says he would pass on a Super Bowl invitation from Jay-Z because he doesn’t think his career fits that stage, not because he wants another rap feud.

The Harlem rapper explained his answer during Talk With Flee, with Cam weighing a hypothetical invitation rather than announcing a booking.

“No. And I don’t mean that in a disrespectful way. I don’t mean that in a disrespectful way. I just don’t think it makes sense,” Cam’ron said when asked whether he would accept a call to perform.

Cam didn’t say Jay-Z had offered him a spot. His answer focused on what he would do if that call came, and he kept the explanation centered on his own suitability for the show.

The distinction between a recognizable rapper and a Super Bowl performer was central to his response. Cam wasn’t saying that a halftime audience would have no idea who he was.

“And I’m not saying people wouldn’t know me, but my career isn’t big enough for that moment,” Cam’ron said.

The comments come as Cam continues explaining how he chooses opportunities beyond recording.

He recently discussed appearing on ESPN’s First Take without taking a fee, describing the exposure as a way to demonstrate his value and draw viewers toward his own programming.

That earlier account put visibility at the center of his decision. His Super Bowl answer takes a different approach: being seen on a huge platform doesn’t automatically make it a performance he wants to pursue.
